<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-systemleastsquarestheorem11-1-orzeroobs-of-equation-blocks">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.SystemLeastSquaresTheorem11_1.orZeroObs_of_equation_blocks</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 11.1</strong> with the displayed equation-specific block design.</p>
<p>This thin wrapper permits equation-specific regressor dimensions, identifies
<code>Q = E[Xᵢ'Xᵢ]</code> with the block-diagonal matrix whose <code>j</code>th block is
<code>E[X_{ji}X_{ji}']</code>, and reuses the observed-row system CLT above. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m : Type u_4} [inst_2 : Fintype m] [inst_3 : DecidableEq m]
  {κ : m → Type u_5} [inst_4 : (j : m) → Fintype (κ j)] [inst_5 : (j : m) → DecidableEq (κ j)]
  {x : Nat → Ω → (j : m) → κ j → Real} {e Y : Nat → Ω → m → Real} {β : Sigma κ → Real},
  HansenEconometrics.SystemObservedResponseFourthMomentConditions μ
      (fun i ω =&gt; HansenEconometrics.systemEquationBlockDesign (x i ω)) e Y β →
    MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution
      (fun t ω =&gt;
        instHSMul.hSMul t.cast.sqrt
          (instHSub.hSub
            (HansenEconometrics.systemLeastSquaresBetaOrZeroObs
              (fun i =&gt; HansenEconometrics.systemEquationBlockDesign (x i.val ω)) fun i =&gt; Y i.val ω)
            β))
      Filter.atTop (fun z =&gt; z.ofLp) (fun x =&gt; μ)
      (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0
        (HansenEconometrics.systemAsymptoticVariance (HansenEconometrics.systemEquationBlockPopulationGram μ x)
          (HansenEconometrics.systemPopulationScoreCovariance μ
            (fun i ω =&gt; HansenEconometrics.systemEquationBlockDesign (x i ω)) e)))</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-11-3">
<summary><span>Theorem 11.3</span><span class="result-count">1 endpoint</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under Assumption 7.2, the robust and homoskedastic system covariance estimators are consistent.</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-systemcovariancetheorem11-3-of-observed-assumption72">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.SystemCovarianceTheorem11_3.of_observed_assumption72</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 11.3</strong> from literal observed-row Assumption 7.2.</p>
<p>The observed-row fourth moments derive all residual-substitution moments in
the compact covariance package. Measurability of both displayed feasible
middle matrices is derived from the observed rows and the Star estimator. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [inst_2 : Fintype k] [inst_3 : DecidableEq k] {m : Type u_4}
  [inst_4 : Fintype m] {X : Nat → Ω → Matrix m k Real} {e Y : Nat → Ω → m → Real} {β : k → Real},
  HansenEconometrics.SystemObservedResponseFourthMomentConditions μ X e Y β →
    And
      (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
        (fun n ω =&gt; HansenEconometrics.systemRobustCovarianceStarObs (fun i =&gt; X i.val ω) fun i =&gt; Y i.val ω)
        Filter.atTop fun x =&gt;
        HansenEconometrics.systemAsymptoticVariance (HansenEconometrics.systemPopulationGram μ X)
          (HansenEconometrics.systemPopulationScoreCovariance μ X e))
      (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
        (fun n ω =&gt; HansenEconometrics.systemHomoskedasticCovarianceStarObs (fun i =&gt; X i.val ω) fun i =&gt; Y i.val ω)
        Filter.atTop fun x =&gt;
        HansenEconometrics.systemAsymptoticVariance (HansenEconometrics.systemPopulationGram μ X)
          (MeasureTheory.integral μ fun x =&gt;
            (fun ω =&gt;
                HansenEconometrics.systemMiddleTerm (X 0 ω)
                  (MeasureTheory.integral μ fun x =&gt; (fun ω =&gt; Matrix.vecMulVec (e 0 ω) (e 0 ω)) x))
              x))</code></pre>
</details>

<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under Assumption 7.2 and (11.8), SUR is asymptotically at least as efficient as system least squares.</p></div>

the observed-row package supplies the primitive Assumption 7.2 facts and

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-11-7">
<summary><span>Theorem 11.7</span><span class="result-count">1 endpoint</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>The reduced-rank normal MLE is characterized by the residualized generalized pencils, least-squares recovery, covariance recovery, and maximized likelihood.</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-reducedrankhansentheorem11-7gaussianmle-residualized-exists">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.reducedRankHansenTheorem11_7GaussianMLE_residualized_exists</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Hansen Theorem 11.7 for residualized multivariate regression, including
existence of the jointly selected primal and dual spectral blocks and the
actual global Gaussian MLE conclusion.</p>
<p>The construction is tie-safe: no separation is assumed between the last
selected root and the first omitted root. The selected-rank premise is the
finite-sample condition ensuring that the positive exact-rank parameter space
has a maximizer rather than only a lower-rank boundary supremum. Positive
definiteness of the unrestricted residual Gram is required only for positive
rank; the rank-zero case is handled directly from the residualized outcome
Gram. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} {m : Type u_4} {ell : Type u_5} [inst : Fintype n] [inst_1 : Fintype k]
  [inst_2 : Fintype r] [inst_3 : Fintype m] [inst_4 : Fintype ell] [inst_5 : DecidableEq n] [inst_6 : DecidableEq k]
  [inst_7 : DecidableEq r] [inst_8 : DecidableEq m] [inst_9 : DecidableEq ell] (Z : Matrix n ell Real)
  (X : Matrix n k Real) (Y : Matrix n m Real)
  [inst_10 : Invertible (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul Z.transpose Z)]
  [inst_11 : Invertible (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul (X.fromCols Z).transpose (X.fromCols Z))]

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-ordered-covmat-maximizes-variance-feasiblebefore-iff-eigenvector">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.ordered_covMat_maximizes_variance_feasibleBefore_iff_eigenvector</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 11.8, optimizer/eigenspace characterization.</strong></p>
<p>For the sequential feasible set, maximizing <code>Var[h'X]</code> is equivalent to lying
in the eigenspace of the <code>j</code>th ordered covariance eigenvalue. The eigenspace
form is the correct statement in the presence of repeated eigenvalues. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {k : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k] {Ω : Type u_3} [inst_2 : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : Ω → k → Real),
  (∀ (i : k), MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun ω =&gt; X ω i) 2 μ) →
    ∀ (j : Fin (Fintype.card k)) (h : k → Real),
      Iff
        (And (HansenEconometrics.pcaFeasibleBefore (HansenEconometrics.orderedPCEigenvector ⋯) j h)
          (∀ (g : k → Real),
            HansenEconometrics.pcaFeasibleBefore (HansenEconometrics.orderedPCEigenvector ⋯) j g →
              Real.instLE.le (ProbabilityTheory.variance (HansenEconometrics.principalComponent g X) μ)
                (ProbabilityTheory.variance (HansenEconometrics.principalComponent h X) μ)))
        (And (HansenEconometrics.pcaFeasibleBefore (HansenEconometrics.orderedPCEigenvector ⋯) j h)
          (Eq ((HansenEconometrics.covMat μ X).mulVec h)
            (instHSMul.hSMul (HansenEconometrics.orderedPCEigenvalue ⋯ j) h)))</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-11-10">
<summary><span>Theorem 11.10</span><span class="result-count">1 endpoint</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>The bias-corrected covariance of iid multivariate-normal rows has Hansen's Wishart law.</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-samplecovariancematrix-haslaw-theorem11-10-wishart">

<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 11.10</strong> in the textbook's literal Wishart notation.</p>
<p>The canonical sample-covariance proof above yields a scaled push-forward law;
<code>scaledWishartLaw_eq_wishartLaw_smul</code> identifies it with
<code>W_m(n-1, (n-1)⁻¹Σ)</code> exactly as displayed by Hansen. </p></div>

          (HansenEconometrics.wishartLaw
            (instHSMul.hSMul (Real.instInv.inv (instHSub.hSub (Fintype.card n).cast 1)) Sigma))
          μ</code></pre>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-11-11">
<summary><span>Theorem 11.11</span><span class="result-count">1 endpoint</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If <code>W</code> is Wishart, then Hansen's inverse-Wishart linear form has the scaled chi-squared law.</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-inversewishartlinearform-haslaw-theorem11-11-raw-of-posdef-card-le">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.inverseWishartLinearForm_hasLaw_theorem11_11_raw_of_posDef_card_le</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 11.11</strong>, raw inverse-Wishart scalar endpoint.</p>
<p>This is the theorem-facing fixed-direction statement: if
<code>W ∼ Wishart_n(Σ)</code>, <code>Σ</code> is positive definite, <code>α ≠ 0</code>, and the Wishart degrees
of freedom dominate the dimension, then <code>(α'W⁻¹α)⁻¹</code> has Hansen's scaled
chi-square law. The proof reuses the standard-coordinate Schur-complement
theorem, canonical rectangular Gaussian Gram nonsingularity, and deterministic
square-root whitening/alignment. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {m : Type u_3} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_1 : Fintype m]
  [inst_2 : DecidableEq m] {dfidx : Type u_4} [inst_3 : Fintype dfidx] (W : Ω → Matrix m m Real)
  (Sigma : Matrix m m Real) (α : m → Real),
  Sigma.PosDef →
    Ne α 0 →
      ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw W (HansenEconometrics.wishartLaw Sigma) μ →
        instLENat.le (Fintype.card m) (Fintype.card dfidx) →
          ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw (fun ω =&gt; HansenEconometrics.inverseWishartLinearForm α (W ω))
            (MeasureTheory.Measure.map
              (fun x =&gt; instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv (dotProduct α ((Matrix.inv.inv Sigma).mulVec α))) x)
              (HansenEconometrics.chiSquared (instHAdd.hAdd (instHSub.hSub (Fintype.card dfidx) (Fintype.card m)) 1)))
            μ</code></pre>
</details>

<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Hotelling's normalized <code>T^2</code> statistic has the <code>F(m,n-m)</code> law.</p></div>

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 11.12</strong>, normalized Hotelling F endpoint.</p>
<p>This is Hansen's normalized form: under iid normal rows with positive-definite
covariance, <code>(n-m)/(m(n-1)) T²</code> has the classical <code>F_{m,n-m}</code> law. </p></div>

<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {m : Type u_3} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [inst_1 : Fintype n] [inst_2 : Fintype m] [inst_3 : DecidableEq m] [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (Y : Ω → Matrix n m Real) (μ0 : m → Real) {Sigma : Matrix m m Real},
  Sigma.PosDef →
    instLTNat.lt 0 (Fintype.card m) →
      instLTNat.lt 0 (instHSub.hSub (Fintype.card n) (Fintype.card m)) →
        (∀ (i : n), ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw (fun ω =&gt; Y ω i) (HansenEconometrics.rowGaussianLaw μ0 Sigma) μ) →
          ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i ω =&gt; Y ω i) μ →

              (HansenEconometrics.classicalFDist (Fintype.card m) (instHSub.hSub (Fintype.card n) (Fintype.card m))) μ</code></pre>
